record.context_brief: Weak unique continuation for p-harmonic functions.
record.original_question: Let 1 < p < infinity, let Omega be a connected open subset of R^n with n >= 2, and let u be a weak solution of the p-Laplace equation div(|grad u|^(p-2) grad u) = 0 in Omega. If u vanishes on a nonempty open subset U of Omega, must u vanish identically on all of Omega?

evidence.quote: Problem 1.1 (Weak unique continuation). Suppose u solves (1.1) and vanishes on a nonempty open set U ⊂ Ω, does u ≡ 0 on all of Ω?
Thus the problem, in both formulations 1.1 and 1.2, remains open in the case n ≥ 3, p != 2.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix an exponent $1 < p < \infty$ and an integer $n \ge 2$. Let $\Omega \subset \mathbb{R}^n$ be a connected open set, and let $u \in W^{1,p}_{\mathrm{loc}}(\Omega)$ be a weak solution of the $p$-Laplace equation
$$\operatorname{div}\bigl(|\nabla u|^{p-2}\,\nabla u\bigr) = 0 \quad \text{in } \Omega,$$
that is, $\int_\Omega |\nabla u|^{p-2}\,\nabla u \cdot \nabla \varphi\, dx = 0$ for every test function $\varphi \in C_c^\infty(\Omega)$.

Suppose there exists a nonempty open subset $U \subset \Omega$ such that $u \equiv 0$ on $U$. Must $u \equiv 0$ on all of $\Omega$?

Resolve this weak unique continuation property, in particular for dimensions $n \ge 3$ and exponents $p \ne 2$.
artifact.status_search_result: The weak unique continuation property for the p-Laplace equation is known to hold in dimension n=2 (work of Manfredi, Alessandrini, and others) and in the linear case p=2 in all dimensions. For n ≥ 3 and p ≠ 2 the question is generally regarded as open. Recent literature (e.g., Granlund–Marola and subsequent work through 2023–2024 on the Almgren-type frequency function for the p-Laplacian) treats it as an outstanding open problem; partial results assume monotonicity/boundedness of a frequency function or additional regularity, but no full resolution has been published.

status_evidence.title: On the problem of unique continuation for the p-Laplace equation
status_evidence.snippet: Studies whether two different solutions of the p-Laplace equation can coincide in an open subset of their common domain; obtains partial results.
status_evidence.claim: Unique continuation for the p-Laplace equation has only partial results in higher dimensions for p ≠ 2.

status_evidence.title: New quantitative uniqueness of continuation for elliptic equations
status_evidence.snippet: Recent (2024) work addressing quantitative unique continuation for elliptic equations, with the nonlinear p-Laplacian case treated as still challenging.
status_evidence.claim: As of 2024 the unique continuation question for the p-Laplacian remains an active research topic without a complete resolution for n ≥ 3, p ≠ 2.
